label: The word ' so' placed right after an action (a verb or its object) or a noun and leading into what follows from it: purpose or result ('she tied the boat up so it would not drift', 'the boiler failed so the school shut'), and also 'so ADJ that' straight after a noun ('a cliff so steep that'). Strongest with no comma before 'so'. Weak (under about 0.3) for 'so' meaning 'very' after is/was/felt ('the tea is so sweet'), weaker for ', so' after an is/was clause, and quiet for fixed phrases ('if so', 'or so', 'even so', 'and so on', 'so-called') and for the same link made without 'so' ('therefore', 'because', 'in order to').
